title: Korean Directors Rally Behind ‘The Assassin(s)’ as Political Firestorm Turns on Its Makers
content:
ByNaman Ramachandran

The Directors Guild of Korea (DGK) has come out in support of the team behind “The Assassin(s),”Hur Jin-ho‘s thriller about the 1974 shooting of first lady Yuk Young-soo, as political anger over the Korean box office leader spills onto its cast and crew.

Conservative politicians and online critics have accused the film of distorting history, and it now faces a police complaint and a fight in the National Assembly.

“What we are facing now is not criticism or condemnation of a film, but attacks on individuals that have crossed the line,” the DGK said in a statement.

The guild said the hostility had moved past questioning the film’s content and its makers’ choices, and “is targeting the daily lives and livelihoods of those who took part, and has gone as far as demanding that such a film never be made again.”

The statement, which named neither Hur nor anyone else, accepted that every film attracts harsh reviews along with praise, and asked who could draw an exact line between fair and excessive criticism.

“Creators can be criticized for their work, but that criticism must not lead to the collapse of the creator’s personal life and livelihood,” the guild said.

The DGK added that its idea of a healthy creative environment includes standing beside filmmakers who want to begin again, because “the chance for that person to start their next story should not disappear simply because a film went through controversy and criticism.”

“The Assassin(s)” opened Sept. 23. Yoo Hae-jin stars as a police inspector who witnesses the Aug. 15, 1974 shooting at the National Theater, where Yuk, the wife of then-President Park Chung-hee, was killed during Liberation Day celebrations, and goes on to lead the investigation. Park Hae-il plays the head of a newspaper’s social affairs desk, and Lee Min-ho a rookie reporter. The official inquiry pinned the killing on Mun Se-gwang alone, saying he acted under instructions from Pyongyang and Chongryon, the pro-North Korean residents’ association in Japan. Hur’s film declines to name a culprit, and its detractors argue the open ending points the finger at Park Chung-hee or his government.

Controversy has not dented the box office. “The Assassin(s)” passed 1 million admissions in four days andled the Korean chart againover the Oct. 2–4 weekend, selling 412,012 tickets from 1,129 screens for a weekend gross of KRW4.07 billion ($3 million). Its running total stands at 2.23 million admissions and KRW21.9 billion ($16.3 million).

The backlash has spread well beyond the film. Rating sites filled up with one-star scores, and the social media accounts of cast members drew abusive comments. Kim Go-eun and Lee Young-ae, who had shared handwritten recommendations, and critic Lee Dong-jin, who had reviewed the film on video, were also targeted. One YouTube film reviewer with 4.17 million subscribers pulled a video about the title.

Lee Jong-bae, a former People Power Party (PPP) Seoul city councilor, has asked Seoul police to investigate Hur, Hive Media Corp. CEO Kim Won-kuk and writers Kwon Ki-jun and Lee Ji-min for defamation. His complaint argues that the plural title invites audiences to suspect a second culprit besides Mun. PPP lawmakers also tried to summon Hur to testify at the annual parliamentary audit, a move blocked by the Democratic Party on creative freedom grounds.

Park Chan-wook, appearing at a Sept. 26 audience Q&A, praised the film as smartly conceived.

In a Sept. 28 statement, the producers had said: “Nowhere in the film is any specific individual defined as being behind the incident, and the film’s hypotheses and dramatic settings are not presented as historical fact.”

The film will open the 37th Singapore International Film Festival on Oct. 21, with Hur due to attend alongside cast members Shim Eun-kyung and Park Sung-hoon. The festival runs through Nov. 1.

“Cinema must carry on as a place where different ideas and voices meet, even when it stirs up debate,” the DGK said. “If that freedom disappears, it becomes hard for new films and new stories to be born.”
title_zh: 韓國導演支持《刺客》(The Assassin(s))，政治風暴轉向其製作人
content_zh:
由納曼·拉馬昌德蘭(Naman Ramachandran)報導

韓國導演協會(Directors Guild of Korea, DGK)已公開支持《刺客(The Assassin(s)》的製作團隊，這部由許秦浩(Hur Jin-ho)執導的驚悚片講述了1974年第一夫人柳永秀(Yuk Young-soo)被槍擊的事件，因為對韓國票房冠軍的政治憤怒已波及其演員和工作人員。

保守派政治家和網上評論者指責該片扭曲歷史，並且目前面臨警方的投訴和國會的抗爭。

DGK在一份聲明中表示：「我們現在面臨的不是對一部電影的批評或譴責，而是對個人的攻擊，這已經越過了界限。」

該協會指出，敵意已經超越了對電影內容和製作選擇的質疑，「而是針對參與者的日常生活和生計，甚至要求這樣的電影再也不要被拍攝。」

聲明中未提及許秦浩或其他任何人，接受了每部電影都會吸引到嚴厲的評價和讚譽，並詢問誰能劃出公平與過度批評之間的確切界線。

「創作者可以因其作品受到批評，但這種批評不應導致創作者的個人生活和生計的崩潰。」該協會表示。

DGK補充說，他們對健康創作環境的理解包括支持那些希望重新開始的電影製作人，因為「那個人開始下一個故事的機會不應因為一部電影經歷了爭議和批評而消失。」

《刺客(The Assassin(s)》於9月23日上映。劉海鎮(Yoo Hae-jin)飾演一名警察檢查官，他目擊了1974年8月15日在國立劇院發生的槍擊事件，當時柳永秀在解放日慶祝活動中被殺，並隨後領導調查。朴海日(Park Hae-il)飾演一家報社社會事務部的負責人，李敏鎬(Lee Min-ho)則是一名新晉記者。官方調查將此案的兇手單獨指向文世光(Mun Se-gwang)，稱他是在平壤和在日本的親北韓居民協會（朝鮮總聯合會）的指示下行動。許秦浩的電影未指名罪犯，其反對者則認為開放式結局暗示了朴正熙(Park Chung-hee)或他的政府。

這場爭議並未影響票房。《刺客(The Assassin(s)》在四天內突破100萬觀影人次，並在10月2日至4日的週末再次登上韓國票房榜，售出412,012張票，來自1,129個銀幕，週末總票房達到40.7億韓元（300萬美元）。目前的總觀影人次為223萬，總票房為219億韓元（1,630萬美元）。

反彈的聲音已經超越了這部電影。評分網站上充斥著一星評分，演員的社交媒體帳號也遭到辱罵。金高恩(Kim Go-eun)和李英愛(Lee Young-ae)曾分享手寫推薦，評論家李東鎮(Lee Dong-jin)也因在視頻中評價該片而成為攻擊目標。一位擁有417萬訂閱者的YouTube電影評論家撤下了關於該片的視頻。

李鍾培(Lee Jong-bae)，前人民力量黨(PPP)首爾市議會議員，已要求首爾警方調查洪( Hur)、Hive Media Corp.執行長金煥國(Kim Won-kuk)以及作家權基俊(Kwon Ki-jun)和李志敏(Lee Ji-min)的誹謗案。他的控訴主張，複數的標題使觀眾懷疑除了文(Mun)之外還有第二個罪犯。人民力量黨的立法委員們也試圖召喚洪出席年度國會審計，但這一舉動因民主黨對創作自由的考量而被阻止。

朴贊郞(Park Chan-wook)在9月26日的觀眾問答環節中讚揚這部電影的構思巧妙。

在9月28日的聲明中，製作方表示：“在電影中，沒有任何具體個體被定義為事件的背後主使，電影的假設和戲劇設定並未被呈現為歷史事實。”

這部電影將於10月21日開幕第37屆新加坡國際電影節，洪將與演員沈恩京(Shim Eun-kyung)和朴成勳(Park Sung-hoon)一同出席。該電影節將持續至11月1日。

“電影必須繼續作為不同思想和聲音相遇的場所，即使這會引發辯論，”DGK表示。“如果這種自由消失，新的電影和故事將難以誕生。”
